original_question: Fix integers n >= 1, b >= 0, and q in [0,n], and consider the Veronese syzygy groups K_{p,q}(n,b;d) = K_{p,q}(P^n, O_{P^n}(b); O_{P^n}(d)) for d large. Theorem 2.1 gives an explicit interval (*) of values of p for which these groups are nonzero. Is that interval exact, meaning that K_{p,q}(n,b;d) = 0 whenever p lies outside the nonvanishing range (*) from Theorem 2.1?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Conjecture 2.3: the claim that the nonvanishing range in Theorem 2.1 is the precise range for Veronese syzygies, i.e. K_{p,q}(n,b;d)=0 outside that interval.
correct_elements: Your draft has the right target and is already very close to the paper. It correctly uses the Veronese notation K_{p,q}(n,b;d)=K_{p,q}(P^n, O_{P^n}(b); O_{P^n}(d)), fixes n, b, q in the correct regime, and asks exactly whether the explicit nonvanishing interval from Theorem 2.1 is sharp by vanishing outside it. That is precisely the content of Conjecture 2.3.
missing_details: The nearest official formulation is Conjecture 2.3 in Section 2, so the question should point to that conjecture rather than only paraphrasing Theorem 2.1.
The interval (*) should be written out explicitly so the question is stand-alone: binom(d+q,q) - binom(d-b-1,q) - q <= p <= binom(d+n,n) - binom(d+n-q,n-q) + binom(n+b,q+b) - q - 1.
The paper does not say only 'for d large' here; in Theorem 2.1 and hence Conjecture 2.3 the explicit hypothesis is d >= b + q + 1.
The ambient ground field in the paper is C; the survey states that it deals throughout with projective varieties over the complex numbers.

To be fully self-contained in the paper's sense, K_{p,q} should be identified as the p-th Koszul cohomology group of weight q, equivalently the space of degree-(p+q) minimal generators in the p-th term of the minimal graded free resolution of R(P^n, O_{P^n}(b); O_{P^n}(d)) over S = Sym H^0(P^n, O_{P^n}(d)).
It should be explicit that p ranges over integers.

The nearby Section 2 context also records the normalization K_{p,q}(n,b;d)=K_{p,q+1}(n,b-d;d), so one may assume 0 <= b <= d-1 when convenient; your draft does not mention this contextual simplification.
If one wants the equivalent complex formulation used in Section 2, one should define S = C[z_0,...,z_n] and S_m as its degree-m piece.
refined_question: Over C, fix integers n >= 1, b >= 0, 0 <= q <= n, and d >= b + q + 1. Let K_{p,q}(n,b;d) := K_{p,q}(P^n, O_{P^n}(b); O_{P^n}(d)), where K_{p,q} denotes the p-th Koszul cohomology group of weight q, equivalently the space of degree-(p+q) minimal generators in the p-th module of the minimal graded free resolution of R(P^n, O_{P^n}(b); O_{P^n}(d)) over S = Sym H^0(P^n, O_{P^n}(d)). Theorem 2.1 proves that K_{p,q}(n,b;d) != 0 whenever binom(d+q,q) - binom(d-b-1,q) - q <= p <= binom(d+n,n) - binom(d+n-q,n-q) + binom(n+b,q+b) - q - 1. Is this range exact, i.e. does one have K_{p,q}(n,b;d) = 0 for every integer p outside this interval?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, with S = C[z_0,...,z_n] and S_m its degree-m piece, Proposition 1.11 and its specialization in Section 2 identify K_{p,q}(n,b;d) with the cohomology at Lambda^p S_d tensor S_{qd+b} of the Koszul-type complex ... -> Lambda^{p+1} S_d tensor S_{(q-1)d+b} -> Lambda^p S_d tensor S_{qd+b} -> Lambda^{p-1} S_d tensor S_{(q+1)d+b} -> ... . Is that cohomology zero for every integer p outside the Theorem 2.1 interval?
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact open problem stated in Section 2: immediately after Theorem 2.1 gives the explicit nonvanishing interval, Conjecture 2.3 asks whether K_{p,q}(n,b;d) vanishes whenever p lies outside that range. This is narrower and more faithful than the general asymptotic-vanishing question from Section 1, because here the paper asks for the full sharp Veronese range, not merely a lower-bound vanishing statement. Definition 1.2 supplies the paper's meaning of K_{p,q}, Proposition 1.11 gives the equivalent Koszul-complex description, and Remark 2.4 records evidence that the conjecture is already known for the extremal weights q=0 and q=n when d is sufficiently large.
